title: Month 5
subtitle: Sitting is coming, and so is the first tooth. The six-month visit is next month.

baby.development: Your baby is rolling both ways, reaching accurately, and may be sitting with their hands propped in front. They are babbling in long strings and copying sounds.

you.body: If you are breastfeeding, supply is stable. If you are pumping at work, output often dips on the days you are stressed, and that is not a supply problem.
you.mind: Five months is often a good month. Sleep may have settled, the baby is fun, and the routine works. Notice it, because the next change is coming.

coreActions.title: Practise sitting with a pillow behind
coreActions.why: Sitting is the skill that unlocks everything after it: reaching, playing, and eventually pulling up.
coreActions.detail: Sit the baby on the floor with a nursing pillow or your legs behind them. Let them prop on their hands. Do not leave them alone, and do not use a seat that holds them upright before they can sit themselves.

coreActions.title: Know the signs of readiness for solids
coreActions.why: The six-month visit is where solids get discussed, and the signs are about skills, not about weight or appetite.
coreActions.detail: Ready means sitting with little support, holding the head steady, and showing interest in food. Tongue thrust that pushes food back out is a sign to wait a few weeks. Most babies are ready between five and seven months.

coreActions.title: Start cleaning the gums and any teeth
coreActions.why: A tooth that arrives and is not cleaned starts the habit of not cleaning it.
coreActions.detail: Wipe the gums with a soft cloth once a day. When a tooth appears, use a soft baby toothbrush with a smear of fluoride toothpaste no bigger than a grain of rice. First dental visit by the first tooth or the first birthday.

alsoKnow.title: Separation anxiety starts around now
alsoKnow.body: A baby who was happy to be handed over may start to cry when you leave the room. It is a sign of attachment, not a sign of a problem, and it peaks between nine and eighteen months.

alsoKnow.title: No water before six months
alsoKnow.body: A baby under six months gets all the water they need from milk. Extra water can dilute their sodium and is not safe. From six months, a small amount in an open cup with meals is fine.

redFlags.text: A fever of 100.4°F or higher with unusual sleepiness or a rash
Fast or labored breathing, or a blue tint around the lips
Feeling hopeless, or thoughts of harming yourself or the baby
